question: In its decision of 21 April 2026 in Case FSP.103117 concerning the procurement of rolling stock for the Lisbon metro (Metropolitano de Lisboa), the Commission accepted commitments under the Foreign Subsidies Regulation1 (FSR), resulting in the replacement of the Chinese supplier CRRC by the Polish manufacturer PESA.

According to publicly available information, the consortium had identified more than one EUbased supplier capable of replacing CRRC. As this was the first remedy procedure to be completed under the FSR, greater clarity is needed regarding the selection process and its implications for future cases. 1.

Was the Commission aware of any alternative FSR-compliant rolling-stock supplier proposed by the consortium, and if so, did it assess that supplier as part of its review; and what was the outcome of that assessment?

Did the Commission’s decision specifically require the appointment of PESA, or did it merely require the replacement of CRRC by an FSR-compliant supplier? If the latter, what factors led to the acceptance of PESA?
Does the Commission intend to publish the non-confidential version of the decision and/or issue guidance on the treatment and selection of replacement suppliers in future FSR remedy procedures?
Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 of 14 December 2022 on foreign subsidies distorting the internal market (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2560/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.7.2026) Pursuant to Article 7(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/25601 (Foreign Subsidies Regulation (FSR)), ‘the Commission may accept commitments offered by the undertaking under investigation where such commitments fully and effectively remedy the distortion in the internal market’.

In this case, the consortium led by Mota-Engil (the Consortium) offered commitments to dispel the concerns the Commission had expressed in the decision opening the in-depth investigation into the case. The Commission conducted a preliminary review of potential alternative subcontractors on the basis of the information submitted by the Consortium for each potential subcontractor.

While the Commission can confirm that the Consortium negotiated with several potential subcontractors, the precise number is confidential and cannot be publicly disclosed. Based on the information received, the Commission could confirm that Pojazdy Szynowe PESA Bydgoszcz Spółka Akcyjna (PESA) had not received foreign subsidies.

This assessment does not prejudge whether foreign subsidies exist in relation to the other potential subcontractors. In this context, the Consortium committed to replace Portugal CRRC with PESA, and the Commission adopted a decision with commitments under Article 31(1) FSR. This decision does not predetermine the outcome of the award procedure.

It is for Metropolitano de Lisboa, the contracting entity, to assess whether the bid of the Consortium complies with all technical and quality requirements set out in the tender documents. The non-confidential version of the Commission’s decision, with any confidential elements redacted, will be published on the Commission’s website dedicated to the FSR in public procurement procedures2 as soon as possible.
1 Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 of 14 December 2022 on foreign subsidies distorting the internal market,
